title: Clare and the monstrance
hookLine: tradition says Clare held up the Eucharist when soldiers attacked her convent

lines: A GOLD SUNBURST ON A STAND.
cards: A statue of Clare of Assisi: a woman in a plain habit, holding a gold sunburst on a stand, with a small round window at the center.
It's a monstrance, the vessel used to show the consecrated host so people can see it and pray. She holds it up, toward something just out of the frame.

Clare was the young woman from Assisi who followed Francis into poverty, and yesterday's song, tradition says, was made in a hut beside her house, San Damiano. So what is just out of the frame? An army.

teach.b: The early Life of Saint Clare tells it. Soldiers serving the emperor, at war in the valley, came to San Damiano, climbed over the walls and got into the cloister. The terrified sisters ran to Clare.
She was sick and could not walk.

teach.h: CARRIED TO THE DOOR, SHE PRAYED.
teach.b: She had herself carried to the door, had the Body of the Lord brought and set in front of her, and lay down before it in prayer.
With the words of a psalm, she asked God not to hand over to beasts the souls that confess to him, and to guard her sisters.

teach.h: A CHILD'S VOICE: I WILL PROTECT YOU.
teach.b: The Life says she heard a voice, like a little child's, promising to protect them always. She asked for the city too, and was told it would suffer but be defended. She turned to the sisters and told them not to be afraid.
The soldiers, the story says, scrambled back over the walls and left. And the vessel?

teach.h: A SILVER BOX, NOT A GOLD SUNBURST.
teach.b: The Life doesn't mention a gold monstrance. It speaks of a small box of silver and ivory, where the host was kept.
The great sunburst belongs to the statues, not to the Life: true to the story's heart, if not to its silverware. Clare didn't wave a weapon or make a speech.
She put the Eucharist between her sisters and the danger, and she held it up.

teach.h: UNLESS THE LORD KEEP THE CITY.
teach.b: The Douay-Rheims psalm puts the idea plainly: "Unless the Lord keep the city, he watcheth in vain that keepeth it."

how: In Catholic churches the consecrated host is placed in a monstrance for adoration and Benediction, and parishes hold hours of Eucharistic adoration when people come to pray before it.

games.why: she was carried to the door, set the Eucharist before her and prayed. the story says the soldiers left.

practice: Walk through your home in your imagination: the front door, the kitchen, the rooms where people sleep, and the people who live there, or used to. Linger at the door.
If you pray, use today's psalm, unless the Lord keep the city, he watcheth in vain that keepeth it; if you don't, simply wish each room well.
